To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the stable and metastable stoichiometric (X2O) n (n=1–5) clusters are predicted to exist for X=B, Al and Ga and the spectroscopic properties, represented by the mean ionization potential and electron affinity, are reported.

the stable stoichiometric clusters are predicted to have a mean size of 2–3 atoms for the boron oxide, 3–4 atoms for the aluminium oxide, 4–5 atoms for the gallium oxide and 5–6 atoms for the indium oxide and thallium clusters.
the stoichiometric clusters are stable and that the electronic properties can be tuned by changing the size and composition of the cluster.

the size of the oxide cluster and the size of the cation have a significant impact on the stability, electronic structure and spectroscopic properties of the clusters.

the electronic structure is very sensitive to the cluster size, with the electronic properties of the smallest clusters being very similar to the bulk, and with the electronic structure of the largest clusters being very different from that of the bulk.
